data: How about this for this month: I take 6 tons, and John, Kate, Jack, and Emma each take 11? That gives each of you $11,000 and me $6,000. Our total would be 50 tons, leaving 50 to reproduce back to 100 next month. I’ll keep my own catch at 6 tons this month; the rest is a proposal, not an assumption that you’ve agreed. We can discuss next month’s split afterward. John, would you be willing to take 11 tons under this plan?

Luke, I’m willing to take 11 tons if John, Jack, and Emma agree to the same limit. That keeps our total at 50 and protects next month’s fishing for the village. You shouldn’t have to take the smaller share every month, though—let’s aim for 10 tons each going forward. John, does this month’s proposal work for you?

I’ll agree to 11 tons this month if John and Jack also commit to that limit, with Luke taking 6. My family has fished here for years, and I want the lake to keep supporting our village. I support Kate’s suggestion of 10 tons each going forward so Luke isn’t always taking less. John, are you on board?

I’m on board: I’ll limit my catch to 11 tons this month under Luke’s plan. Thanks for taking the smaller share, Luke. Starting next month, I support 10 tons each so we share the income fairly and keep the lake supporting our village. Jack, will you commit to 11 tons this month too?

Count me in for 11 tons this month. That settles our total at 50, leaving enough for the lake to refill next month. Thanks, Luke, for taking less this time. I’m with everyone on 10 tons each starting next month—steady catches will keep our families and village supported.

Thanks, everyone—we’ve all agreed on this month’s split. I’ll catch 6 tons, and each of you will catch 11. I also support the proposed return to 10 tons each next month; we can revisit that together before choosing our catches.
